Package org.aeonbits.owner.formats.yaml

Class YamlLoader

java.lang.Object
org.aeonbits.owner.formats.yaml.YamlLoader
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Loader
public class YamlLoader extends Object implements Loader
A loader for YAML, reading a source whose path ends in .yaml or .yml. 
     server:
       host: localhost
       port: 8080
     servers:
       - host: alpha
       - host: beta
     ports: [80, 443]
 
     server.host=localhost
     server.port=8080
     servers[0].host=alpha
     servers[1].host=beta
     ports[0]=80
     ports[1]=443

The keys are the ones every loader here flattens to, so a YAML document is read by the same nested interfaces, indexed lists and grouped maps as anything else.

It is a subset, and this is the whole of it

Read: block mappings and sequences nested by indentation, a mapping opened on the same line as its dash, plain and quoted scalars, the block scalars | and > with their chomping indicators, flow collections, comments, and a leading ---.

Refused by name, with the line they are on — never guessed at, because guessing changes what a file means rather than declining to read it:

  • anchors, aliases and merge keys — &name, *name, <<:
  • tags — !!str, !Ref
  • complex keys — ?
  • a value continued on the next line without | or >
  • a second document in the same file
  • a tab used as indentation, which YAML forbids and which no two editors agree about

Types are not guessed

A scalar is kept exactly as it was written, and what it means is decided by the method that reads it. That is what spares this parser YAML's implicit type resolution — the Norway problem, where no becomes false and the country code of Norway stops being a string — and it is also the honest arrangement: the interface is where the types are declared, so the interface is where they should be decided.

The consequence is worth stating: enabled: yes is the text yes, and a method returning boolean will read it through the ordinary conversion rather than through YAML 1.1's table. Write true when a boolean is meant.

What an absent value produces

host: with nothing after it, ~ and null are the same thing and write no key at all, as in JSON and for the same reason: a Properties cannot hold a null. An empty flow sequence writes an empty value, which is already read as an empty collection; an empty mapping writes nothing, a section with nothing in it having nothing to say.

    • defaultSpecFor

      public String defaultSpecFor(String urlPrefix)
      Description copied from interface: Loader
      Returns the default URI specification for a given URI resource, that can be handled by this loader.

      Returning null means this loader adds nothing to the sources looked for in the absence of @Sources - which is what SystemLoader and DotEnvLoader both do, since neither is named after the configuration interface. That is also why this method has a default: it is a choice a loader is allowed to decline, and declining it should not require writing a method that returns nothing.

      A loader offering more than one name - a format spelled .yaml and .yml, or .ini and .cfg - overrides Loader.defaultSpecsFor(String) instead. The two are not meant to be overridden together.

      Specified by:
      defaultSpecFor in interface Loader
      Parameters:
      urlPrefix - the prefix identifying the URI resource.
      Returns:
      the default URI specification for a given URI resource, or null for none.

    • defaultSpecsFor

      public String[] defaultSpecsFor(String urlPrefix)
      Description copied from interface: Loader
      Returns every default URI specification this loader offers, and is the one the library calls.

      The default answers with whatever Loader.defaultSpecFor(String) returned, so a loader with a single name has nothing to do here and a loader written before this method existed keeps working unchanged. Override this one, and not that one, when a format goes by several names: 

           @Override
     public String[] defaultSpecsFor(String uriPrefix) {
         return new String[] { uriPrefix + ".yaml", uriPrefix + ".yml" };
     }

      The order matters: these are tried in the order given, and under Config.LoadType.FIRST the first one that resolves is the one that answers. An empty array, like a null from the single-valued method, means this loader adds nothing.

      Specified by:
      defaultSpecsFor in interface Loader
      Parameters:
      urlPrefix - the prefix identifying the URI resource.
      Returns:
      the default URI specifications, in the order they should be tried; never containing null.
